rationale: Checked one more premise while the run has time left, and recorded it as a negative result rather than a claim. liveBootstrap installs a bootstrap configuration by calling BootstrapCluster and then processConfigurationLogEntry, so the node ends with the new configuration as its latest one and the empty previous configuration as its committed one, with committedIndex zero. That looked like it could let a snapshot record an empty configuration, since takeSnapshot refuses only when the FSM's applied index is behind committedIndex. Tracing the rest shows it cannot: takeSnapshot needs the FSM to have applied an entry, applied entries require a commit, and any commit index at or above latestIndex makes appendEntries replace the committed configuration with the latest one, so the committed configuration is fixed before the first snapshot can carry an index. The sources for that ordering are recorded with this update, along with the two configuration sources already in the index. No defect is asserted and no execution is requested; the five questions and their accounts are unchanged.

knowledge.statement: A live-bootstrapped node cannot write a snapshot carrying an empty committed configuration, even though liveBootstrap leaves the new configuration as latest with the empty previous configuration as committed at index zero. takeSnapshot requires the FSM to report an applied index and refuses only when that index is behind committedIndex, so a snapshot needs an applied entry; entries are applied only after a commit; and appendEntries replaces the committed configuration with the latest one whenever the committed index reaches latestIndex. The committed configuration is therefore corrected at the first commit, before any snapshot index exists that could record it.
knowledge.conditions: A node bootstrapped through BootstrapCluster or liveBootstrap in this implementation, with snapshots requested through the FSM path; single-voter or multi-voter, since the argument only uses the ordering of commit and snapshot availability.
